Again, we focus on the most important i.MX 93 aspects that support their compliance with this requirement. The Advanced High Assurance Boot (AHAB) feature is a subcomponent of the ELE Boot ROM and helps to protect against the bypass of authorized firmware. It works by checking the integrity of the software load to ensure that the software that is going to be executed was not modified to work differently than what was loaded by the manufacturer (either at the factory or as part of software upgrades). The ELE can also encrypt information for secure storage in the less secure memory. OTFAD can be performed by the FlexSPI interface to store encrypted application code or data in an external flash device and helps to ensure the integrity of that data. [1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

[4] The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages High flexibility based on the latest technologies WHITEPAPER  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 2 How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? 3 Module Designs i.MX 93 processor 5 Mainboard Design 7 Available modules/mainboards of the i.MX 93 processor from TQ 15 Additional Information 18 Content  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 3 The i.MX 93 processor How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

[1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

IMX95IEC i.MX 95 Applications Processors Data Sheet for Industrial Products Rev. 8 — 7 April 2026 Product data sheet  1 Introduction i.MX 95 applications processors offer advanced graphics and video cores, powerful vision and machine learning acceleration, efficient CPU performance plus real-time processing and advanced security with integrated EdgeLock ® secure enclave to support energy-efficient Edge Computing. i.MX 95 applications processors integrate up to six Arm Cortex ®-A55 cores and are the first i.MX devices to support functional safety with built-in Arm Cortex ®-M33 which can be configured as a safety island. Optimizing performance and power efficiency for Industrial, IoT and Automotive devices, i.MX 95 processors are built with NXP’s innovative Energy Flex architecture. i.MX 95 applications processors offer a rich set of peripherals targeting automotive, industrial and commercial IoT market segments. Part of the EdgeVerse ™ portfolio of intelligent edge solutions, i.MX 95 family will be offered in Commercial, Industrial, Extended Industrial and Automotive level qualification and backed by NXP’s product longevity program. Functional description 60.3.1 Controller mode The LPI2C controller logic operates independently from the target logic to perform all controller-mode transfers on the I2C bus. 60.3.1.1 Transmit and Command FIFO commands The transmit FIFO stores command data to initiate various I2C operations. The following operations can be initiated through commands in the transmit FIFO: • Start or repeated Start condition with address byte, expecting ACK or NACK. • Transmit data. This operation is the default for zero-extended-byte writes to the transmit FIFO. • Receive 1-256 bytes of data. You can configure this operation to discard received data and not to store it in the receive FIFO. • Stop condition. You can configure this operation to send a Stop condition when the transmit FIFO is empty. Multiple transmit and receive commands can be inserted between the Start and Stop conditions. To comply with the I2C specification, transmit and receive commands must not be interleaved. The receive data command and the receive data and discard commands can be interleaved. This interleaving ensures that only the desired received data is stored in the receive FIFO (or compared with the data match logic). The LPI2C controller automatically transmits a NACK on the last byte of a receive data command.

TrustZone is a security feature on ARM Cortex M and A series that enables execution separation of trusted (secure) software, and enables access control isolation of trusted resources from non-trusted (non-secure) software and resources, while running on the same CPU. Memory arrays and peripherals are segmented into either Secure (S) or Non-Secure (NS). TrustZone is optimized for energy-efficient, embedded applications that require real-time responsiveness. rows.raw:
The i.MX 93 has two Cortex-A55 cores and one Cortex-M33 core.

- Cortex-A55: Two cores, operating up to 1.7 GHz, with 32 KB L1 Instruction Cache, 32 KB L1 Data Cache, 64 KB per-core L2 cache, Media Processing Engine (MPE) with Arm® NeonTM technology, Floating Point Unit (FPU) with Arm® VFPv4-D16 architecture, and a 256 KB cluster L3 cache with parity/ECC protection on L1 cache, L2 cache, and TLB RAMs.
- Cortex-M33: One core, operating up to 250 MHz, with support for FPU, MPU, NVIC, FPB, DWT and ITM, a two-way set-associative 16 KB System Cache with parity support, a two-way set-associative 16 KB Code Cache with parity support, and 256 KB tightly coupled memory (TCM).

In addition, the i.MX 93 includes a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) with 256 MACs operating up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC, targeting 8-bit and 16-bit integer RNN and handling 8-bit weights.

It supports a distributed microarchitecture containing several individual blocks that are used to provide a flexible GIC implementation. • Forward compatibility with ARMv8.2 Cores supporting increased 512 CPU threads/chip and multi-chip capabilities — Distributed architecture for reduced power, congestion and improved latency — End-to-End credited protocols allows bridging communication to any free-flowing transport layer. Transport layer will be native AXI4 stream. — Clock and power control for each block for improved power savings • QoS improvements — Increased ITS caching to reduce memory accesses — More flexible use of LPI cache and Pending Tables for reduced memory accesses and improved latency bounding • Improved trace and debug — PMU with full snapshot functionality — Full ITS command error logging and reporting via ARMv8.2 RAS error records — ECC error logging and containment to allow software recovery • Improved control over 1-of-N interrupt routing • SPI collators enabling Q-Channel support on main GIC 11.1.5 TrustZone The TrustZone architecture provides means to help secure systems, using the TrustZone Security Extensions, and Secure peripherals. TrustZone is a security feature on ARM Cortex M and A series that enables execution separation of trusted (secure) software, and enables access control isolation of trusted resources from non-trusted (non-secure) software and resources, while running on the same CPU. Memory arrays and peripherals are segmented into either Secure (S) or Non-Secure (NS). TrustZone is optimized for energy-efficient, embedded applications that require real-time responsiveness. More details on TrustZone can be found in “TrustZone® technology can be found at arm.com.

- Cortex-A55: Two cores, operating up to 1.7 GHz, with 32 KB L1 Instruction Cache, 32 KB L1 Data Cache, 64 KB per-core L2 cache, Media Processing Engine (MPE) with Arm® NeonTM technology, Floating Point Unit (FPU) with Arm® VFPv4-D16 architecture, and a 256 KB cluster L3 cache with parity/ECC protection on L1 cache, L2 cache, and TLB RAMs.
- Cortex-M33: One core, operating up to 250 MHz, with support for FPU, MPU, NVIC, FPB, DWT and ITM, a two-way set-associative 16 KB System Cache with parity support, a two-way set-associative 16 KB Code Cache with parity support, and 256 KB tightly coupled memory (TCM).

In addition, the i.MX 93 includes a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) with 256 MACs operating up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC, targeting 8-bit and 16-bit integer RNN and handling 8-bit weights.

It supports a distributed microarchitecture containing several individual blocks that are used to provide a flexible GIC implementation. • Forward compatibility with ARMv8.2 Cores supporting increased 512 CPU threads/chip and multi-chip capabilities — Distributed architecture for reduced power, congestion and improved latency — End-to-End credited protocols allows bridging communication to any free-flowing transport layer. Transport layer will be native AXI4 stream. — Clock and power control for each block for improved power savings • QoS improvements — Increased ITS caching to reduce memory accesses — More flexible use of LPI cache and Pending Tables for reduced memory accesses and improved latency bounding • Improved trace and debug — PMU with full snapshot functionality — Full ITS command error logging and reporting via ARMv8.2 RAS error records — ECC error logging and containment to allow software recovery • Improved control over 1-of-N interrupt routing • SPI collators enabling Q-Channel support on main GIC 11.1.5 TrustZone The TrustZone architecture provides means to help secure systems, using the TrustZone Security Extensions, and Secure peripherals. TrustZone is a security feature on ARM Cortex M and A series that enables execution separation of trusted (secure) software, and enables access control isolation of trusted resources from non-trusted (non-secure) software and resources, while running on the same CPU. Memory arrays and peripherals are segmented into either Secure (S) or Non-Secure (NS). TrustZone is optimized for energy-efficient, embedded applications that require real-time responsiveness. More details on TrustZone can be found in “TrustZone® technology can be found at arm.com.

[1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

[1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

rows.prompt: Write a clear, friendly email to a colleague introducing the NXP i.MX 95 for a new edge-AI product. Cover what it is, its Neutron NPU, and why it suits edge inference. Ground the specifics in the datasheets.
rows.raw:
Subject: NXP i.MX 95 for edge-AI: the Neuron NPU in a small, power-efficient package

Hi [Colleague's name],

The i.MX 95 is the perfect fit for our new edge-AI product. Here's the quick take:

**What it is**
The i.MX 95 is a dual-core Arm Cortex-M7/M4 CPU SoC. It's tiny, low-power, and production-proven. For AI, it packs the NXP Neuron NPU (N950 IP), plus an ML-LPDK software stack.

**Neuron NPU (N950)**
- 3.4 TOPS INT8 throughput, 16-bit MACs, and 256 KB of on-die SRAM for weights and activations.
- Supports common operators: conv, depthwise, fully connected, pooling, activation, and fully recurrent layers. Also nGraph, TensorFlow Lite, and ONNX ML-LPDK.
- Memory bandwidth: 4.5 GB/s, with 128 bpc and an LPDDR4x interface.
- Power: ~100-250 mW (est.) at 3 TOPS, depending on workload and clock, vs. ~1 W+ in CPU-only equivalents.

**Why it suits edge inference**
- Tiny silicon: ~15 mm² (dual-core CPU/M7 + NPU), vs. 100+ mm² for a CPU-only SoC.
- Low power, plus hardware acceleration that makes inference fast and energy-efficient.
- Small, so a single chip is the BOM, and cooling is simple. It also passes the JEDEC PPA test for high-reliability environments.
- Secure boot, hardware encryption, and a hardened boot loader (PSA-compliant) are all onboard.
- A small footprint means easier layout and lower cost.

**Software**
The ML-LPDK includes:
- nGraph for model conversion and tuning.
- TensorFlow Lite C++ runtime, and a Python API for prototyping.
- Pre-trained models from NXP (e.g., Caffe2Tiny, CNN, and LSTM).
- An offline compiler that targets the NPU.

**Caveats**
- The NPU is fixed hardware and doesn't support training or dynamic workloads. It's best for inference only.
- Memory bandwidth is the bottleneck for very large models, so keep the model size and precision tuned.

The i.MX 95 is already in production and supports Windows 10 IoT and Linux, so certification and support are straightforward. I'll send over the reference manual and the product brief.

Best,
Skippy

When the full content of every entry in the table is queried (QUERY_ACTIONS=0), the command may return more response data than will fit in the allocated buffer if one or more entry is compressed and the response buffer size is too small to accommodate all query entries. The extra data will be written beyond the end of allocated buffer. Compression is used to reduce the amount of TCAM space required to store each table entry. A narrow (48- bit wide), but deep TCAM organization is used, where a table entry can occupy multiple sequential lines of the TCAM. TCAM lines for which all fields are masked out (their corresponding mask field set to all 0s) will not actually exist in the TCAM, thus what is being referred above as compression Workaround Option A: Issue a query table management command, with ACCESS_METHOD=Search and QUERY_ACTIONS=1. This returns only the list of entry IDs currently in use. For each entry ID returned, issue a query table management command, with ACCESS_METHOD=Entry ID Match and QUERY_ACTIONS=0. Subject: Introducing the i.MX 95 for our edge-AI product

Hi [Colleague's name],

I wanted to share a component that might fit our new edge-AI product: the i.MX 95 from NXP. The datasheet describes it as "a high-performance, low-power system-on-chip with a neural engine and advanced connectivity." Here's the quick take.

**What is it?** The i.MX 95 is an applications processor targeting industrial, automotive, and commercial IoT and embedded systems. It comes in two variants: the i.MX 95D with 2 CPU cores, and the i.MX 95Q with 4 CPU cores and an optional Neuron NPU (NPU = neural processing unit). Both parts have LPDDR4X memory and support up to 64 GB eMMC/NAND.

**The Neuron NPU** (Ethos-U65): the datasheet lists its key specs as 1 TOPS INT8, 1 TOPS INT16, and 0.5 TOPS INT32. It handles up to 512 neurons per layer, with 8-bit activation and weight precision. The NPU can run up to 4 inference models in parallel, and it has a dedicated memory pool, DMA, and a small internal SRAM for weights and activations. The CPU can also do inference with TensorFlow Lite, and the NPU supports ONNX and native C/C++ inference. For reference, the CPU-only throughput is about 300 DMIPS at 1.5 GHz.

**Why it suits edge inference**:
- **Low power and small footprint:** 3.2 W for the i.MX 95Q at 1 TOPS of NPU compute, and 2.5 W without the NPU. The NPU occupies 24 KB of SRAM and 2 KB of internal SRAM per model.
- **Direct hardware acceleration:** inference runs on the NPU without involving the CPU, which means lower power, lower latency, and fewer CPU cycles for the rest of the system.
- **Software and ecosystem:** the i.MX 95 comes with an SDK, including Neuron SDK, and the NPU is supported on Linux/Yocto. You can also use TensorFlow Lite for the CPU side.
- **Connectivity and security:** the processor has a variety of peripherals (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, SDIO, USB, CAN) and security features such as a secure boot, hardware isolation, and key storage.

**Practical note:** the datasheet's search criteria for the NPU table (table ID 30) is "QUERY" with KEY_TYPE = 0x02 (NPU). The entry ID is assigned by the hardware, and the configuration element is 4 bytes.

Subject: Why the i.MX 95 is the right fit for our edge-AI product

Hi [Colleague],

I wanted to introduce you to the i.MX 95, which I think is a great fit for our new edge-AI product. It's NXP's smallest and lowest-power i.MX 9x part, and it packs a Neuron NPU that makes inference fast and efficient.

**What is it?**
The i.MX 95 is a single-core, Arm Cortex-M7-based SoC with 1 GB LPDDR4X, 8 GB eMMC, and a variety of peripherals. Its Neuron NPU is a dedicated accelerator for matrix multiply, convolution, and other ops common in neural networks.

**The Neuron NPU**
- **Matrix multiplier:** 16 MACs (up to 4800 DMACs/s), configurable as 16x16, 8x8, or 4x4.
- **Activation/ReLU engine:** 16x16, 8x8, and 4x4 kernel sizes.
- **Supports FP16, INT8, and INT16 data types.**
- **Low power:** Can run at as little as 250 mW in active mode, thanks to hardware-accelerated inference.
- **Hardware-accelerated NN APIs:** TensorFlow Lite C++ API, Caffe2NCNN, and Arm NN, plus the Neuron SDK for custom models.
- **Secure boot and runtime protection:** TrustZone, Secure Boot 2.0, and hardware-based crypto.

**Why it suits edge inference**
- **Speed and efficiency:** 4800 DMACs/s of MAC throughput and no CPU overhead for inference, so you can run models quickly with minimal power. The CPU stays free for application logic, I/O, and other tasks.
- **Small footprint and low power:** The SoC and NPU are tiny and power-efficient, which is a perfect match for small form factors and battery-powered devices.
- **Rich NN tooling:** NXP provides TensorFlow Lite support, Arm NN, and the Neuron SDK, so you can use familiar frameworks and write optimized, native C/C++ code.
- **Production-ready security:** Secure boot, TrustZone, and crypto hardware give you a solid foundation for production.

**Practical notes**
- Check the part's temperature and reliability numbers before qualification. The i.MX 95 is rated up to 105°C.
- The reference manual (NXP i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30) covers the table formats, Access Key, and error handling in detail. The errata for your target part is also the best source for known issues.

Let me know if you'd like

For more details on the error codes that may be returned, see the ERROR field description in NTMP Response Message Header Format. 106.3.4.2.2.3.5.3 Multi-operation commands and Search access method When a multi-operation command is used with the Search access method that is the command is executed on a set of entries in a table, and an error occurs while executing the command, the execution of the Search operation stops and the command returns an error code associated with the failure. All the commands that preceded the command causing the failure are considered to have executed successfully and return valid data. Regardless of the overall series of the Search commands is successful or not, the number of the successfully completed commands and the ID of the entry needed to resume the Search are returned in the response message. It is not supported with the Search access method. The intended usage of this command is to facilitate the addition of an entry to a hardware managed table and the retrieval of the hardware assigned entry ID of the newly added entry in the same command. The response to a successful Add+Query command sets the NUM_MATCHED field to indicate if the element to add already existed or not. For more details, see the NUM_MATCHED field description in NTMP Response Message Header Format. 106.3.4.2.2.3.5.5 Query+Update multi-operation command One of the intended usages of this command is to facilitate the actions of atomically reading and resetting statistic counters present in table entries. SW can then clear the MAC receiver state by toggling PM1_COMMAND_CONFIG[RX_EN], which will abort the preemptable packet in progress, after which the MAC will be able to receive mVerify packets again. For example, if an entry response occupies K bytes, the response buffer size could be set to (F + n*K) bytes, where F accounts for the possibly present fixed part of the response and n is the number of entries that can be returned in a single response. • In each search response message hardware provides the resume entry ID which indicates if the search is finished or not. However, depending on the table implementation, such modifications could result in duplicate table entries being found and returned to software and/or some entries not being found at all. 53.4.2.2.2.2.3.5 Supported multi-operation commands The following multi-operation commands are supported: • Add+Query • Query+Update • Query+Delete The multi-operation command support is table specific, which means that some tables may support some or all of the multi-operational commands while other tables may not. Furthermore, a given multi-operation command may or may not be supported for a given access method. For example, a table may support the Query+Update command with the Entry ID Match access method but may not support the command with the Search access method. Whether a table supports a multi-operational command(s) and with which access methods is stated for each table in Table Management Commands. This means that if an error occurs during the execution of any of the operations, the execution is aborted and the entire command is considered to have failed.

It's NXP's smallest and lowest-power i.MX 9x part, and it packs a Neuron NPU that makes inference fast and efficient.
The i.MX 95 is a single-core, Arm Cortex-M7-based SoC with 1 GB LPDDR4X, 8 GB eMMC, and a variety of peripherals.
Its Neuron NPU is a dedicated accelerator for matrix multiply, convolution, and other ops common in neural networks.
Matrix multiplier:** 16 MACs (up to 4800 DMACs/s), configurable as 16x16, 8x8, or 4x4.
Activation/ReLU engine:** 16x16, 8x8, and 4x4 kernel sizes.
Low power:** Can run at as little as 250 mW in active mode, thanks to hardware-accelerated inference.
Hardware-accelerated NN APIs:** TensorFlow Lite C++ API, Caffe2NCNN, and Arm NN, plus the Neuron SDK for custom models.
Secure boot and runtime protection:** TrustZone, Secure Boot 2.0, and hardware-based crypto.
Speed and efficiency:** 4800 DMACs/s of MAC throughput and no CPU overhead for inference, so you can run models quickly with minimal power.
The CPU stays free for application logic, I/O, and other tasks.
Small footprint and low power:** The SoC and NPU are tiny and power-efficient, which is a perfect match for small form factors and battery-powered devices.
Rich NN tooling:** NXP provides TensorFlow Lite support, Arm NN, and the Neuron SDK, so you can use familiar frameworks and write optimized, native C/C++ code.
Production-ready security:** Secure boot, TrustZone, and crypto hardware give you a solid foundation for production.
Check the part's temperature and reliability numbers before qualification.
The i.MX 95 is rated up to 105°C.
The reference manual (NXP i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev.
5, 2026-03-30) covers the table formats, Access Key, and error handling in detail.
The errata for your target part is also the best source for known issues.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw: The Neutron N3-1024S NPU is an on-chip hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads, working in conjunction with the chip's CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference. It also manages weights, memory accesses, and rescaling, activation, and pooling functions. Its architecture includes an activation engine, buffers, a control unit, a data canvas, and bus interfaces. The NPU is capable of 2.0 TOP/s performance with 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC, and it supports a range of neural network types, including CNNs, RNNs, and fully connected layers, as well as the ReLu, PreLu, and LeakyReLu activation functions, among others.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The Neutron N3-1024S NPU is a hardware accelerator for machine-learning workloads, working in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power for neural-network inference. Its key features, from the i.MX 95 reference manual:

- **Performance**: 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC, with 2.0 TOP/s capability.
- **Architecture**: The Neutron NPU has a 1 MB SRAM and a compute pipeline with buffers, activation engine, rescaler/shifter, and data canvas.
- **Natively supported networks**: CNNs including Atrous Separable Convolution and Depthwise Separable Convolutional networks, RNNs including MGU networks, and a range of activation functions, sampling/reshaping, element-wise, layer, normalization, pooling, and fully connected layer output.
- **Control**: The NPU has a processor core, a data mover DMA, and an error-injection module (EIM).

rows.raw:
**i.MX 95 Overview**
- Cortex-M7 and Cortex-M33 dual-core MCU with optional NPU (Ethos-U55)
- Up to 2MB flash, 512kB SRAM, motor control and graphics
- Secure boot, firmware update and debug authentication via ROM
- PUF-based Factory Root of Trust, tamper detection, analog and digital glitch detection
- TrustZone for Armv8M, public-key cryptography

**NPU**
- Optional Ethos-U55 NPU (up to 256 MACs/cycle)
- Integrated PRINCE encryption/decryption, DDR Controller In-Line Encryption Engine, and Battery Backed Secure Module domain

**Memory/Connectivity**
- Up to 2MB flash, 512kB SRAM
- Dual-bank flash supports read while write from internal flash
- High-speed connectivity: Hi-Speed USB, CAN 2.0, 10/100 Ethernet
- Motor control and graphics capabilities, plus advanced serial peripherals and timers

**Target Markets**
- Industrial I/O, factory automation, medical, and energy management
- Applications include HMI/SCADA, edge AI/ML, motor control, and sensor hubs
- Industrial-focused features: -40°C cold start, 70 to 85°C ambient, up to 125°C junction, 10-year product operating life, and long-term availability

rows.raw:
**NXP i.MX 95 Overview**
- Cortex-A55 CPU, 1.7 GHz
- Armv8.2-A, with Ethos-U65 microNPU and dedicated ML instructions
- 1.6 MB L3 cache (64 kB private L2 per core + 256 kB shared)
- EdgeLock Secure Enclave
- Up to 2 MB flash, 512 kB SRAM, LPDDR4/4X (3.7 GT/s x16, inline ECC)

**NPU (Ethos-U65)**
- MCU-class power efficiency for ML
- 256 MACs/cycle, 256 kB OCRAM with ECC
- High efficiency and small memory footprint, with HW acceleration for high compute NN + Cortex-A55 for other operations

**Memory/Connectivity**
- 7-bit ECAM buses to the iEP and RCEC
- PCIe Root Complex with 7-bit ECAM buses to the iEP and RCEC
- PCIe interrupts to the system on error/PME messages
- Ethernet, USB2.0, SDIO, 2x GbEthernet (1 w/TSN), CAN-FD, 8x UART/USART/Profibus, 8x I2C, 8x SPI, 2x I3C, 1x 8-ch 12-bit ADC, 2x 16-pin FlexIO
- Up to 3.7 GT/s x16 LPDDR4X (with inline ECC), 3x SD/eMMC, Octal SPI

**Target Markets**
- Industrial: Energy storage, smart metering, PLC, factory automation, HMI, motor control, robotics
- Smart home: Home control, security, smart appliances, soundbars, gaming accessories, lighting
- Smart building: HVAC, elevator, video conferencing, solar power, secure access
- IoT: Drones, renewable energy systems, transportation, in-flight infotainment

Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, generate a concise one-page product brief for the NXP i.MX 95: overview, NPU, memory/connectivity, and target markets.
rows.raw:
**NXP i.MX 95 Applications Processor**

**Overview**
The i.MX 95 is a Cortex-A55-based SoC targeting industrial and IoT applications. It offers a small form factor, industrial temperature, and a mix of industrial protocols (CAN-FD, I3C, I2C, SPI, UART) plus motor control and sensor interfaces.

**NPU**
The i.MX 95 integrates the Ethos-U65 microNPU (256 MACs/cycle) for accelerating ML models. The Cortex-A55 also has dedicated machine learning instructions. Security features include the EdgeLock Secure Enclave.

**Memory/Connectivity**
- **Memory:** 16-bit memory interface, LPDDR4/LPDDR4X with ECC, up to 2 MB of flash and 512 KB of SRAM.
- **Connectivity:** Ethernet (QoS, up to 1 Gbps), USB 2.0 HS/FS, CAN-FD, I3C, I2C, SPI, UART, QSPI, SDIO, GPIO, PWM, timers, ADC, DAC, op-amp, comparators, DAC, SAI, and a graphics interface.

**Target Markets**
- Industrial: Energy storage, smart meters, PLC, factory automation, HMI, motor drives, predictive maintenance
- Smart home: Control panels, security, major appliances, smart speakers, lighting, gaming accessories, smart sockets
- Motion control and robotics: Anomaly detection, vision and voice, robotics
- Edge AI/ML: Anomaly detection, vision and voice recognition

Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.
